gen.title: How steady speed and time set flight distance

cards.stem: How is the maximum distance an aircraft can fly calculated?
options: ground speed times the maximum time (tmax)
twice the distance flown
extra fuel for climbing to altitude
cards.quote: The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).

cards.stem: What is the combat radius for a round trip mission?
options: half of the range
ground speed times the maximum time (tmax)
wind speed is constant
cards.quote: The combat radius would be half of the range as specified here.

cards.stem: When does ground speed stay constant during cruise?
options: wind speed is constant
the thrust is equal to the drag
half of the range
cards.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.

cards.stem: What force balance keeps an aircraft in steady level flight?
options: the lift is equal to the weight
drag then slows the airplane
weight constantly changes as fuel is burned
cards.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.
